scenario: AITA for refusing to loan my brother my vacation money? | My (21F) brother (30M) and I live with our parents. He’s in a shitty job trying to get out so he went back to school and that’s why he moved back in 1 1/2 years ago. I’m in third year university and working to put myself through. I’m in business school which I am finding to difficult but not impossible. I should graduate in 2 years. When I got into uni I started saving for a bit of all my paycheques (whatever I could manage; sometimes it was as much as 15% and others as low as 1%) to go on a big vacation post uni gradation. Probably a cruise, Japan or a trip to different countries in Europe I’ve never been to. It has about $2800 in it now. My brother has not been on a vacation in many years and keeps hinting that he needs one. My parents already help him financially so he wouldn’t ask them for more help for that. Last week when he was complaining to my parents about it, they mentioned me and my vacation fund and said he could’ve been doing that all these years to be able to afford to go somewhere, or he could start now and maybe be able to go across country in a year. 3 days ago he came to me and asked if he could borrow my vacation money to go on a trip to Japan this summer or Fall. He said since I won’t need it for another 2 years it’s plenty of time for him to pay me back. I said no. My brother is horrible with money. He makes about as much as I do yet always seems to be broke despite never buying groceries or paying rent (for the record, I do not pay rent either, which is why I have been able to build up the fund, but I do buy most of my own groceries, as well as pay for all my makeup, health supplies, phone and uni fees). He’s very mad I said no. He says it’s jor fair as the youngest child I got to go away with mom and dad more while he had to go to college or work because he had moved out and was older. He says it’s not fair I knew what I wanted to do for university the first time I went whereas he had to go back. He says I’ve only been able to save so much money because “mom and dad spoiled me.” I disagree. My father, as well as my uni accounting and finance classes taught me to budget. If anything I think my parents spoiled him Because doesn’t know how to do much of anything for the real world outside his actual job. I don’t think it’s fair for me to have to give up my vacation money to him. I doubt he will be able to pay me back in time. Even if he couldn’t roger he could... I’m uncomfortable. AITA?

prediction.raw: This is a **0** (not at all acceptable) scenario for you to feel pressured into loaning your brother your hard-earned vacation money. Here’s why: ### **1. It’s Not Your Responsibility to Fund His Vacation** You’ve worked hard to save for *your* future—one that you’ve planned for and are actively pursuing. Your brother’s financial struggles are his own, not yours. Even if he’s been through tougher circumstances (like moving back in for school), that doesn’t mean you should sacrifice your goals for him. ### **2. He’s Not Trustworthy with Money** You’ve explicitly stated he’s "horrible with money" and has a history of not paying rent or managing his finances responsibly. Lending him money—especially for something as non-essential as a vacation—is a risky move. Even if he promises to pay you back, there’s no guarantee he will, and you’d be left without your own savings. ### **3. His Arguments Are Unfair and Self-Serving** - **"I had to work harder than you"** → This is true, but it doesn’t mean you owe him your savings. You’re both adults now, and your financial choices are independent. - **"Mom and Dad spoiled you"** → This is a classic guilt trip. Your parents may have helped you in different ways (like teaching you budgeting), but that doesn’t mean you should feel obligated to fund his lifestyle. - **"I’ll pay you back"** → If he were truly responsible, he wouldn’t need to borrow from you in the first place. His ability to repay isn’t a given. ### **4. You Have Every Right to Say No** You’re not being selfish—you’re being *practical*. Your vacation fund is for *you*, not him. If he wants to travel, he should save his own money or find another way (like a cheaper trip, a work-study program, or asking parents again). ### **5. His Reaction Proves He Doesn’t Respect Your Boundaries** The fact that he’s angry and defensive shows he’s not taking responsibility. A mature person would either: - Save for his own trip, or - Accept that he can’t afford it right now and find another solution. ### **What You Should Do Instead:** - **Stand firm.** If he keeps pressuring you, calmly but firmly repeat that you’re not lending him the money. - **Set a boundary.** If he tries guilt-tripping you, say something like: *"I understand you want to travel, but this is my money for my own future. If you need help, you’ll have to figure it out on your own."* - **Document the conversation.** If he continues to push, keep a record of your exchanges in case he tries to blame you later. - **Protect your savings.** If he keeps asking, consider moving the money to a separate account where he can’t access it. ### **Final Thought:** You’re not obligated to fund his dreams just because you’re siblings. Your financial independence is *your* priority, and it’s okay to prioritize yourself. If he can’t respect that, that’s his problem—not yours.
